📆
On October 15, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov
will take part
in
the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia
(
#CICA
) in Baku.
The event will address CICA’s continued development
, including its role in the broader framework of cooperation between platforms across Eurasia.
Discussions will cover a wide range of areas of practical cooperation on CICA’s agenda
, including support for small and medium-sized enterprises and international information security, both coordinated by Russia.
Participants will also exchange views on
current international and regional issues
.
🌐
CICA comprises 28 countries
: Russia, Azerbaijan, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bahrain, Vietnam, Egypt, Israel, India, Jordan, Iraq, Iran, Kazakhstan, Cambodia, Qatar, Kyrgyzstan, China, Kuwait, Mongolia, the UAE, Palestine, Pakistan, the Republic of Korea, Tajikistan, Thailand, Turkiye, Uzbekistan and Sri Lanka.
The Summit is expected to approve Laos’s accession as a full member
.
Observers
(Belarus, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, Turkmenistan, the Philippines,
the League of Arab States
,
the International Organization for Migration
and the UN) and
partner organisations
(
the Economic Cooperation Organization
,
the SCO
,
the SCO Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure
and
the UN Office on Drugs and Crime
)
have also been invited
.
The Summit’s agenda will focus on ensuring sustainable development in the region and strengthening connectivity across the continent
, as well as countering emerging challenges and threats, including those in international information security.
During the event, the Russian Side intends to draw its partners’ attention to
the transformation of the system of international relations as a new, more just
#MultipolarWorld
order takes shape.
📃
The Summit is expected to adopt
a general political declaration
and
a thematic document on improving occupational safety standards
.
***
🇷🇺
Russia has been a CICA member since its inception.
Russian proposals and projects within the association seek to promote cooperation based on equality and mutual benefit, with a focus on tangible results.
In 2021, Russia’s proposal to include cooperation on international information security in the CICA Catalogue of Confidence Building Measures was endorsed
. Russia coordinates cooperation in this area.
We regularly hold seminars on the sustainable development of the Internet, security in the use of ICTs and efforts to counter their use for criminal purposes.
☝️
Russia promotes the preservation of historical memory within CICA.
At Moscow’s initiative,
a ministerial statement marking the 80th anniversary of Victory in World War II

#WeRemember
📅
#OTD
in 1943, an uprising broke out at
#Sobibor
— the only successful mass escape by POWs from Nazi “death factories” during
#WW2
.
The
Sobibor uprising was helmed by
Alexander Pechersky,
a Soviet POW, lieutenant of the Red Army, held among others in Sobibor. The
Soviet officer performed a truly heroic feat
— just in a few weeks, he managed to devise an escape plan, rally other prisoners and inspired them to fight the Nazis.
◼️
During
#WWII
, Germany established around 14'000 'death camps'. Among them, the so-called
death factories
became infamous as places where the Nazis herded their victims
for the one purpose — annihilation.
Sobibor was among such “death factory”, established in the south-east of Nazi-occupied Poland, near the Western Bug River and the Polish-Soviet border. The camp was built alongside the railway line between the towns of Chełm and Włodawa.
POWs were transported to Sobibor in entire railway carriages,
for one sole purpose — to be killed
. The camp was turned into a veritable 'assembly line' for the
mass murder of human beings.
Each and every day, up to six trains carrying POWs arrived at Sobibor, including prisoners of war and civilians — elderly people, women and children.
At Sobibor, the Nazis
starved their victims and exploited them to death
. Inhuman medical experiments were conducted on POWs. People from
Austria
,
Czechoslovakia
,
France
and other countries were brought to the camp to be tortured. In June 1943, two special trains carrying children arrived at Sobibor from the
Netherlands
. In September 1943, a group of Soviet POWs arrived from the Minsk transit camp.
According to various estimates, the Nazis exterminated up to 250'000 POWs at Sobibor during the camp’s existence.
🎖
From the all-Union newspaper '
Krasnaya Armiya
' (
The Red Army
)
(September 2, 1944):
The Nazis turned Poland into one vast prison, where millions of people from every country in Europe perished after indescribable suffering.
<...>
The Sobibor camp was one of the death factories established by the Germans on Polish territory. Residents of the Polish village of Zhlobok-2 <...> wrote in a letter to the Red Army command that the inhabitants of villages neighbouring Sobibor knew well of the conditions in this horrific concentration camp.
Every day, more than 1'000 people of various nationalities were exterminated in the camp’s gas chambers. <...>
The Germans referred to this camp as a “button factory” and a “thread factory”...
***
⚔️
On 14 October 1943, an uprising broke out at Sobibor under the leadership of lieutenant
Alexander Pechersky.
The POWs, who dared to challenge the enemy,
engaged in an unequal battle
. Overpowering 'SS' guards with their bare hands, prisoners rushed towards the main gate despite machine-gun fire from the watchtowers.
❗️
Nothing could stop exhausted people determined to break free from Nazi enslavement.
As a result of the uprising, around 300 people managed to
escape from the sheer hell on earth
. Many of those who survived and made it to freedom joined the resistance movement and continued fighting the Nazis.
Pechersky himself joined the Belarusian partisans
and, in 1944, returned to the front, fighting the enemy as part of an assault battalion.
The
#
SobiborUprising
became a testament to the unbending human will and strength of spirit — a symbol of
the triumph of good over Nazi evil
.
The crimes committed at Sobibor formed part of the charges brought against the Nazis at the
Nuremberg Trials
.
In March 1962, eleven guards who had served at
Sobibor
and
Treblinka
stood trial in Kiev. Alexander Pechersky himself testified as a witness.
All the Nazi criminals were sentenced to death.
Today, the
Alexander Pechersky Foundation
, together with the
Russian Military Historical Society
, museums and other organisations, is doing everything possible to ensure that the
memory of the heroic feat
of the Sobibor prisoners is
carefully preserved
and passed on to future generations.
#LestWeForget
#Victory81

item.title: ⚡️ On October 13, the Belgian Ambassador to Russia, Michel Gerebtzoff, was summoned
item.description: ⚡️ On October 13, the Belgian Ambassador to Russia, Michel Gerebtzoff, was summoned to the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Belgian diplomat was informed that the Russian Side resolutely rejects the increasingly frequent and wholly unfounded assertions by the Kingdom’s military and political leadership concerning growing hybrid and sabotage threats, alongside direct military threats to Belgium and Europe purportedly emanating from Russia. It was emphasised that the overtly aggressive statements by certain representatives of the Belgian authorities, who deliberately portray Russia as an enemy, contribute to a further escalation and increase the risk of the confrontation they are stoking spiralling out of control. ❗️ The Belgian Side was urged to consider the consequences of such statements and to rein in its anti-Russian rhetoric , which is fuelling a further rise in tensions on the European continent.

🔹
We received this information with outrage.
By deliberately denying visas to our top gymnasts seeking to
participate in the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships (Rotterdam, October 17-25, 2026), the Dutch authorities have once again demonstrated their utter disregard for one of the fundamental principles of international sport - fair play. This is clearly a deliberate attempt to weaken our team through political and bureaucratic means.
🔹
I personally visited the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs
, where I strongly urged the authorities to honour their obligations as the host country of an international sport event and ensure that all Russian gymnasts receive the necessary documents to participate.
🔹
Instead, I was presented with utterly unconvincing arguments that defy any reasonable criticism. We were told that visa applications would supposedly be assessed by the Netherlands in light of the "potential negative impact of the participation of Russian champions on international relations". Such position is simply impossible to justify or explain in any rational terms.
🔹
With this decision, The Hague has not only discredited itself
by denying entry to Angelina Melnikova, Viktoria Listunova and Anna Kalmykova, but has also put the organisers in an extremely difficult position. Without the participation of the strongest athletes, one can hardly speak of a fully representative World Championship. Spectators have been deprived of the opportunity to enjoy performances by internationally acclaimed gymnasts, while athletes from other countries have been denied the chance to test their skills against the true leaders of world gymnastics.
🔹
Ultimately, everyone has lost. The responsibility for casting a shadow over what should be a celebration of sport, bringing people together rather than dividing them, rests entirely with the Dutch authorities. They sought to "teach Russia a lesson", but have only demonstrated that the Netherlands cannot be trusted to host major international sport events.

, including by striking vessels and port infrastructure involved in military logistics.
I would like to emphasise that, as long as only the Russian-flagged vessels and foreign vessels operating in the interests of Russian economic operators were targeted in the Black Sea,
freedom of navigation was not widely covered either by the West or the relevant international organisations
. <...>
Our
counterattacks
which targeted exclusively facilities linked to the Kiev regime’s military-industrial complex have come as
a painful blowback for Kiev
. This explains why Zelensky and his handlers are seeking ways to mitigate the intensity of Russian military strikes. Their objective is clear: under the formal pretext of concern for global food security,
they seek to secure a protected maritime route for supplying the Ukrainian military with weapons
and to create yet another instrument for exerting political and economic pressure on Russia. <...>
As we know from our own experience, concluding memorandums and declarations without establishing effective implementation mechanisms is unlikely to meaningfully improve the situation.
Kiev regularly violates the agreements it signs
. <...>
Consider, finally, the Black Sea Grain Initiative of 2022-2023, which
NATO countries used as a cover for supplying weapons to the Ukrainian military
. <...>
Those now calling for achieving normalised navigation in the Black Sea are overlooking the key point: the current food security challenges are
a direct consequence of Kiev’s actions
, while its sense of impunity and the absence of consequences stem from the West’s irresponsible policies. <...>
Russia is a responsible and, without any exaggeration, critical participant in the global food market.
Ukraine’s share of that market, by contrast, should not be overstated
. To give just two examples, Russia accounts for around 26 percent of global wheat exports, compared with just 6 percent for Ukraine, and 20 percent of barley exports, compared with 5 percent for Ukraine.
☝️
Moreover, up to 70 percent of Ukrainian agricultural products go
primarily to the EU and other Western countries
that are by no means poor. <...>
Our friends and partners from the Global Majority countries know that
Russia has never shied away from substantive dialogue on promoting global food security
.
We are convinced that, at this stage, the most effective immediate measure would be to exert collective international pressure on Kiev as the main source of instability. This could produce more tangible results in the near term.

#Victory81
🌟
On October 13, 1944,
#Riga
— the capital of the Latvian Soviet Socialist Republic — was liberated by from Nazi occupation.
Following a rapid advance towards the city and fierce combat on the outskirts of Riga, units of the Red Army’s 2nd and 3rd Baltic Fronts — commanded by Generals Andrey Yeremenko and Ivan Maslennikov, respectively,
victoriously entered Riga
.
🎖
A significant contribution to the defeat of the Nazi troops occupying Riga was made by
Latvian national units within the Red Army
— notably the soldiers of the 130th Latvian Rifle Corps. They fought bravely against the Nazi invaders,
helped liberate our common Motherland
and, through joint efforts, brought the Victory closer.
***
#NoStatuteOfLimitations
Riga remained under Nazi German occupation from July 1941. Over the three years of occupation, tens of
thousands of civilians were killed by the Nazis,
including effectively the entire Jewish population of Riga. The Nazi occupants plundered local resources and exploited the population to meet the needs of the Wehrmacht.
Located some 18 kilometres from Riga was the Nazi
#
Salaspils
concentration camp
—
a sinister “death factory” where 12'000 children of various ages were killed.
Thousands of them perished.
The camp claimed the lives of more than 100'000 people, including children, civilians and prisoners of war, who died from starvation, medical experiments, gas chambers and disease.
#ArchivesSpeak
◼️
Learn more about Nazi crimes at Salaspils
◼️
Nazi atrocities in the occupied Latvian SSR
***
On 13 October, the people of Riga welcomed Soviet liberators
.
📄
From a report submitted to the Head of the Political Directorate of the 3rd Baltic Front, dated October 13, 1944:
The city’s population — workers, the urban poor, office employees and intellectuals — welcomed our forces with great joy and sincere affection.
The people of Riga greeted soldiers and officers with flowers, red flags and portraits of the leaders of our Party and Government.
The liberation of Riga was one of the most difficult operations
conducted by the Red Army in this sector of the front. The enemy fought fiercely for the city, turning it into a fortress. Riga — served as the administrative centre of the Nazi 'Reichskommissariat Ostland', one of the Third Reich’s key military and political hubs in Eastern Europe.
📄
From a report by the head of the Political Department of the 43rd Guards Latvian Rifle Division:
The division fought its way from the borders of the Latvian SSR to Riga, yet nowhere had the local population welcomed us more warmly than in Riga itself…
The city’s residents greeted the soldiers and officers with flowers and red flags.
#WeRemember
Around 150'000 Soviet soldiers and officers lost their lives in the liberation of Latvia.
In memory of the Red Army soldiers, a
monument to the Liberators of Riga from the German Fascist Invaders was opened in central Riga.
This iconic memorial in the capital’s Victory Park became an enduring
symbol of the triumph over Nazism in the Baltic region
, as well as a tribute to the gratitude of the republic’s residents for the heroic sacrifice of Soviet soldiers.
❌
In the summer of 2022, the Latvian authorities ordered the
demolition of the renowned monument,
in what was a
👉
flagrant act of historical revisionism and state-sponsored vandalism
. For decades, it had been a major memorial site for hundreds of thousands of compatriots and Latvians who cherished the historical truth.
The aim of this act of barbarism, driven by anti-Russian sentiment among Latvia’s political establishment, was to
erase from the memory of generations the historical truth about the heroic feat of the Soviet soldiers-liberators,
who, at the cost of immense sacrifice and effort, saved the peoples of the Baltic region from destruction and ruthless Germanisation under the Reich.
❗️
But
#WeRemember
and
#LestWeForget

item.title: 🇷🇺 On October 13, President of Russia Vladimir Putin and President of the United Arab Emirates Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇦🇪 📞 On October 13, President of Russia Vladimir Putin and President of the United Arab Emirates Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan had a telephone conversation . With this year marking the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Russia and the UAE , the Presidents discussed ways to expand strategic and mutually beneficial bilateral cooperation. During their exchange of views on international affairs, they discussed the agreements reached during Vladimir Putin’s telephone conversation with US President Donald Trump regarding Russian diesel fuel supplies , as well as prospects for resolving the crisis in the Persian Gulf region . 🤝 The Presidents agreed to continue their personal contacts. #RussiaUAE
